Senses.Explanation: A verb phrase: “awaken” plus “the Way.” Chan records use it retrospectively in biographies and cases: Lingyun awakens on seeing peach blossoms, the Buddha on seeing the morning star, and other monks after an encounter or event; verses composed afterward are called “verses on awakening to the Way.” The stock pairing “awaken to the Way on hearing a sound; clarify mind on seeing a form” is itself raised and questioned in a hall address. The records also police the designation: one text calls memorizing two convenient sayings and naming that “awakening to the Way” one of the enumerated kinds of foolish Chan. Thus the term names an attested event and biographical verdict, while the corpus also records challenges to loose claims of it.

Senses.Explanation: A solitary buddha (pratyekabuddha) is a named class of awakened figure placed beside hearers, bodhisattvas, and buddhas in the records. The witnesses use the figure in ranked lists, scripture quotations raised inside Chan records, and masters’ contrasts; they do not supply an independent life story. Dahui compares the merit of solitary-buddha attainment with the first arousal of resolve, while Huangbo includes attaining the solitary-buddha fruit in a warning about attachment to meritorious roots. Zen bends the inherited category by putting it to work in live appraisal and contrast. The entry does not infer that every solitary buddha teaches, refuses to teach, or belongs to the ancestral lineage.
